section: Part I, Chapter 2 — Adam's Disobedience and the Knowledge of Good and Evil
subtitle: דלאלהֵ אלחאירין — The Guide of the Perplexed
author: Moses Maimonides (1138–1204)
intro: A learned man once put a sharp objection to Maimonides: if Adam gained the knowledge of good and evil only by eating from the tree, how can that knowledge be at once his sin's punishment and his crowning perfection? Maimonides answers by drawing the distinction that runs through the whole Guide — between the intelligibles (true and false), grasped by intellect, and the merely accepted (fine and base), the realm of opinion into which Adam fell when he turned from intellect to appetite. Hover a phrase to see its English light up; tap any word for a gloss; dotted words are key terms.

terms.note: The conventionally 'fine' and 'base' (ḥasan / qabīḥ) — propositions everyone grants but which reason neither proves nor refutes. Maimonides' key move: before the fall Adam lived among the intelligibles (maʿqūlāt), where things are simply true or false; eating from the tree plunged him into the mashhūrāt, the realm of mere opinion about good and evil.

terms.gloss: the intelligibles — what reason knows as true or false
terms.note: Necessary truths apprehended by the intellect, where the categories are 'true' and 'false' (emet / sheqer), not 'fine' and 'base.' One does not say the sphericity of the heavens is 'fine' or the flatness of the earth 'base' — only true or false. Adam's original perfection lay wholly here.

The intellect that God made to emanate upon man — his 'final perfection' and the imago Dei. Adam possessed it whole before the fall; his disobedience stripped (salaba) it from him, and in its place came the apprehension of mere opinion.

terms.gloss: to cause to emanate; the overflow (of intellect) from God
terms.note: The Neoplatonic-Aristotelian language of emanation: the intellect is not man's own achievement but a fayḍ, an overflow, that God 'made to flow' upon him. Its loss is therefore a withdrawal of something divine.
Adam's God-given natural constitution, paired here with his 'intelligibles' as the state on account of which it was said 'Thou hast made him but little lower than God.'

The act of the tree. Maimonides insists it was not a gaining of intellect but a turning away from it toward 'imaginative appetites and bodily pleasures' — so that the 'knowledge' Adam acquired was a fall, not an ascent.

Here the test case is elohim, applied alike to God, to angels, and to magistrates who govern cities — which is why Onqelos could render 'you shall be as elohim' as 'you shall be as rulers.' Recognizing the equivocity is the first step in dissolving the objection.

The pull of imagination and the bodily senses — 'that the tree was good for food and a delight to the eyes.' To incline toward these is, for Maimonides, the very content of Adam's sin and the cause of his loss of intellect.

pairs.ja: וקצד נחו אלשי אלד'י כאן אלאמר תקדם אליה באן לא יקצדה
pairs.en: and made for the very thing he had earlier been commanded not to make for
he was driven out of the Garden of Eden

aligned.ja: וד'לך הו אלעקאב אלנט'יר ללמעציה, מדה כנגד מדה.
aligned.en: And that is the punishment that answers to the transgression, measure for measure.

pairs.en: And that is the punishment that answers to the transgression
measure for measure

aligned.ja: לאנה בוח פי אלאכל מן אלאטיאב ואלאלתד'אד' בראחה וטמאניה; פלמא שרה ותבע לד'אתה וכ'יאלאתה, כמא קלנא, ואכל מא נהי ען אכלה, מנע מן אלג'מיע.
aligned.en: For he had been given leave to eat of the good things and to enjoy them in ease and tranquility; but when he grew greedy and followed his pleasures and his fancies, as we have said, and ate of what he had been forbidden to eat, he was barred from it all.

pairs.ja: לאנה בוח פי אלאכל מן אלאטיאב
pairs.en: For he had been given leave to eat of the good things
and to enjoy them in ease and tranquility
but when he grew greedy and followed his pleasures and his fancies
as we have said
and ate of what he had been forbidden to eat
he was barred from it all

aligned.ja: ולזמה אכל אכ'ס אלמאכל אלתי לם תכן לה קבל בגד'א, בעד אלתעב ואלנצב, כמא קאל וקוץ ודרדר תצמיח לך וכו', בזעת אפך וכו'.
aligned.en: And he was bound to eat the meanest of foods — which had not been his food before — and to do so only after toil and labor, as it says, 'thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee' (Gen 3:18), and so forth, 'in the sweat of thy face' (Gen 3:19), and so forth.

pairs.en: And he was bound to eat the meanest of foods

pairs.ja: אלתי לם תכן לה קבל בגד'א
pairs.en: which had not been his food before
and to do so only after toil and labor

pairs.ja: כמא קאל וקוץ ודרדר תצמיח לך
pairs.en: as it says, 'thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee'
in the sweat of thy face

aligned.ja: ובין וקאל וישלחהו י״י אלהים מגן עדן לעבד את האדמה.
aligned.en: And it explained further, saying, 'so the Lord God sent him forth from the Garden of Eden, to till the ground' (Gen 3:23).

pairs.en: And it explained further, saying

pairs.ja: וישלחהו י״י אלהים מגן עדן לעבד את האדמה
pairs.en: so the Lord God sent him forth from the Garden of Eden, to till the ground

aligned.ja: וסואה באלבהאים פי אגד'יתה ואכת'ר חאלאתה, כמא קאל ואכלת את עשב השדה.
aligned.en: And it made him the equal of the beasts in his food and in most of his states, as it says, 'and thou shalt eat the grass of the field' (Gen 3:18).

pairs.en: And it made him the equal of the beasts
in his food and in most of his states

pairs.ja: כמא קאל ואכלת את עשב השדה
pairs.en: as it says, 'and thou shalt eat the grass of the field'

aligned.ja: וקאל מבינא להד'ה אלקצה: אדם ביקר בל ילין נמשל כבהמות נדמו.
aligned.en: And, explaining this whole matter, it said: 'man that is in honor and understands not is like the beasts that perish' (Ps 49:13).

pairs.ja: אדם ביקר בל ילין נמשל כבהמות נדמו

aligned.ja: פסבחאן ד'י אלמשיה אלתי לא תדרך גאיתהא וחכמתהא.
aligned.en: Glory be to the Possessor of the Will, whose purpose and wisdom cannot be grasped!
